AssignASVs

Shawn Xinyu Wang

April 15, 2025

Set up the environment

Set seed

set.seed(20020206)

Load packages

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, dada2,
               patchwork, DT, install = FALSE)

Load filtered fastq files

# place filtered seq filed into a variable
filtered_fastqs_path <- "data/02_Filtered_fastqs/"

# Intuition check
filtered_fastqs_path
## [1] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs/"
# Create forward vector
filtered_forward_reads <-
  list.files(filtered_fastqs_path, pattern = "_1_filtered.fastq.gz",
             full.names = TRUE)

# Check
filtered_forward_reads[1:5]
## [1] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060060_1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [2] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060061_1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [3] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060062_1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [4] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060065_1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [5] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060066_1_filtered.fastq.gz"
# Create forward vector
filtered_reverse_reads <-
  list.files(filtered_fastqs_path, pattern = "2_filtered.fastq.gz",
             full.names = TRUE)

# Check
filtered_reverse_reads[1:5]
## [1] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060060_2_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [2] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060061_2_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [3] "data/02_Filtered_fastqs//SRR13060062_2_filtered.fastq.gz"

Sample Names

# Create vector of sample names from the filenames 
sample_names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(filtered_forward_reads), "_"), `[`,1) 

# Intuition Check 
head(sample_names)
## [1] "SRR13060060" "SRR13060061" "SRR13060062" "SRR13060065" "SRR13060066"
## [6] "SRR13060067"
# Forward Reads
error_forward_reads <-
  learnErrors(filtered_forward_reads, multithread = 12)
## 102186000 total bases in 486600 reads from 18 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
# Plot
forward_error_plot <-
  plotErrors(error_forward_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Forward Read: Error Model")
forward_error_plot
## Warning in scale_y_log10(): log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

# Reverse Reads
error_reverse_reads <-
  learnErrors(filtered_reverse_reads, multithread = 12)
## 102582960 total bases in 854858 reads from 33 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
# Plot
reverse_error_plot <-
  plotErrors(error_reverse_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Reverse Read: Error Model")
reverse_error_plot
## Warning in scale_y_log10(): log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

# Look at the plots together
forward_error_plot + reverse_error_plot
## Warning in scale_y_log10(): log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.
## log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

What are the current ASV lengths?

  1. What is the sequencing strategy?
    • paired-end 2×150 bp Illumina HiSeq
  2. What’s the total length of our starting amplicons?
    • 515F-806R region
    • 806−515=291bp
  3. What is the ASV length without primers?
    • 515F primer is 19 bp, and the 806R primer is 20 bp.
    • 291−19−20=252bp
  4. What is the length of the trimmed ASVs after filterAndTrim()?
    • trimLeft=0, no base at the beginning is removed, still 252bp
  5. What is the overlap between our forward and reverse reads?
    • In the actual data, the forward sequence is 150bp and the reverse sequence is 230bp. After Trim, it is 140bp and 220bp.
    • Overlap=220+140−252=108bp

INTERPRETATION #1: The hypothesized ASV length for this dataset is 232 bp. This is based on the following considerations: (1) The sequencing strategy used was paired-end 2×150 bp Illumina HiSeq. (2) The total length of the starting amplicons, targeting the 515F-806R region, is 291 bp. (3) After removing the 515F (19 bp) and 806R (20 bp) primers, the expected ASV length without primers is 232 bp. (4) Since trimLeft = 0, no bases were removed from the start, and the ASV length remains 252 bp after filterAndTrim(). (5) The actual sequence lengths after trimming are 210 bp (forward) and 130 bp (reverse), resulting in an overlap of 108 bp, which is sufficient for accurate merging.

Infer ASVs

# Forward ASVs
dada_forward <-
  dada(filtered_forward_reads,
       err = error_forward_reads,
       multithread = 12)

Merge Forward and Reverse ASVs

  mergePairs(dada_forward, filtered_forward_reads,
             dada_reverse, filtered_reverse_reads,
             verbose = TRUE)

Create a rough

# Raw ASV
raw_ASV_table <- makeSequenceTable(merged_ASVs)

# Check
dim(raw_ASV_table)
## [1]  173 3086
typeof(raw_ASV_table)
## [1] "integer"
class(raw_ASV_table)
## [1] "matrix" "array"
# Write out raw_ASV_table
write.table(raw_ASV_table, file = "data/01_DADA2/raw_ASV_counts.tsv",
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)

Assess the ASV Length

# Creating a table to inspect the distribution of ASV lengths
table(nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table)))
## 
##  232  233  234 
##  352 2705   29
#Plot
plot_ASVLength_raw <-
  data.frame(ASV_Length = nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ASV_Length)) + 
  geom_histogram() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(220, 245)) +
  labs(title = "Raw ASV Lengths",
       y = "Number of ASVs", x = "ASV Sequence Length (bps)")
print(plot_ASVLength_raw)
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_bar()`).

INTERPRETATION #2: The expected length of the ASV is 232 bp, and in fact almost all ASVs are 233 bp, which is in line with expectations.

Trim ASVs

# Only pull ASVs that have a length of 233 bps
raw_ASV_table_trimmed <-
  raw_ASV_table[,nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table)) == 233]
#raw_ASV_table_trimmed

# Intuition Check
table(nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table_trimmed)))
## 
##  233 
## 2705
#Plot
plot_ASVLength_trimmed <-
  data.frame(ASV_Length = nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table_trimmed))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ASV_Length)) + 
  geom_histogram() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(220, 245)) +
  labs(title = "Trimed Raw ASV Lengths",
       y = "Number of ASVs", x = "ASV Sequence Length (bps)")
print(plot_ASVLength_trimmed)
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.

## (`geom_bar()`).

INTERPRETATION #3: Remove all ASVs that are not 253 bp.

Remove Chimeras

noChimeras_ASV_table <-
  removeBimeraDenovo(raw_ASV_table_trimmed,
                     method = "consensus",
                     multithread = 12,
                     verbose = TRUE)
## Identified 1498 bimeras out of 2705 input sequences.
# Structure of data
dim(noChimeras_ASV_table)
## [1]  173 1207
dim(raw_ASV_table_trimmed)
## [1]  173 2705

What proportion is left of the sequences?

Chimera removal compared to trimming

percRetained_chimerasTrimmed <- sum(noChimeras_ASV_table)/sum(raw_ASV_table_trimmed) # Chimera removal compared to raw
percRetained_chimerasRaw <-sum(noChimeras_ASV_table)/sum(raw_ASV_table)

# Plot it 
maxLength_ASV <- max(nchar(getSequences(noChimeras_ASV_table)), na.rm = TRUE)
plot_ASVLength_NoChimeras <- 
  data.frame(Seq_Length_NoChim = nchar(getSequences(noChimeras_ASV_table))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Seq_Length_NoChim )) + 
  geom_histogram()+ 
  # include the x-axis scales
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(220, maxLength_ASV + 12)) + 
  labs(title = "Post-Chimera ASV Lengths",
       y = "Number of ASVs \n (Post-Chimera Removal)", 
       x = "ASV Sequence Length (bps)")

# A little function to identify number seqs 
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))

# Make the table to track the seqs 
track <- cbind(sapply(dada_forward, getN),
               sapply(dada_reverse, getN),
               sapply(merged_ASVs, getN),
               rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table))

colnames(track) <- c("denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")
rownames(track) <- row.names(noChimeras_ASV_table)

# Generate a dataframe to track the reads through our DADA2 pipeline
track_counts_df <- 
  track %>%
  # make it a dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_names")

# Now let's add a column for the number of ASVs
# First, intuition check that the samples match 
stopifnot(track_counts_df$sample_names == row.names(noChimeras_ASV_table))

# Now, let's add a new column with the number of ASVs
track_counts_df <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  mutate(num_ASVs = rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table > 1))

# Visualize it in table format 
DT::datatable(track_counts_df)
# Plot it!
track_counts_df %>%
  pivot_longer(denoisedF:nochim, names_to = "read_type", values_to = "num_reads") %>%
  mutate(read_type = fct_relevel(read_type, "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = read_type, y = num_reads, fill = read_type)) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = sample_names), color = "grey") + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") + 
  labs(x = "Filtering Step", y = "Number of Sequences") + 
  theme_bw()

plot_ReadDepth <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = nochim)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  labs(x = "Total # of Sequences", y = "# of Samples") + 
  theme_bw()

# What is the ASV richness per sample? 
plot_ASVRichness <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num_ASVs)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  labs(x = "Total # of ASVs", y = "# of Samples") + 
  theme_bw()

# Now, let's look at the relationship of ASVs and Sequencing depth 
plot_ReadDepth_ASVRichness <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = nochim, y = num_ASVs)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  labs(x = "Total # of Sequences", y = "# of ASVs") + 
  theme_bw()

# Show the plots together 
plot_ReadDepth + plot_ASVRichness + plot_ReadDepth_ASVRichness + 
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.

INTERPRETATION #5: 1, The distribution appears roughly unimodal, centered around 10,000–25,000 reads per sample. 2, The ASV richness is also unimodal, mostly falling within 25 to 100 ASVs per sample.Some samples show higher ASV richness (~125 ASVs), while a few have low richness (< 25 ASVs). 3, There appears to be a positive correlation between sequencing depth and ASV richness, but the trend is not perfectly linear.

# Transpose abundance table so ASVs become rows
asv_table <- t(noChimeras_ASV_table)

# Assign 4-digit ASV IDs like ASV_0001, ASV_0002, ...
asv_ids <- sprintf("ASV_%04d", seq_len(nrow(asv_table)))
rownames(asv_table) <- asv_ids

# Save cleaned ASV table
write.table(asv_table,
            file = "data/01_DADA2/ASV_table.tsv",
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE)

#  Extract ASV sequences and create DNAStringSet
asv_seqs <- colnames(noChimeras_ASV_table)
asv_dna <- DNAStringSet(asv_seqs)

#  Create 4-digit ASV IDs and assign as names to the sequences
asv_ids <- sprintf("ASV_%04d", seq_along(asv_seqs))
names(asv_dna) <- asv_ids  # Assign ASV IDs as sequence names for output consistency

#  Assign taxonomy using SILVA training set
taxa_silva <- dada2::assignTaxonomy(
  asv_dna,
  "data/silva_db/silva_nr99_v138.1_train_set.fa.gz",
  multithread = TRUE
)

#  Add species-level annotation using species assignment file
taxa_silva_species <- dada2::addSpecies(
  taxa_silva,
  "data/silva_db/silva_species_assignment_v138.1.fa.gz"
)

#  Fix overwritten rownames caused by addSpecies()
rownames(taxa_silva_species) <- names(asv_dna)

#  Convert to data frame, move ASV ID column to front
taxa_df <- as.data.frame(taxa_silva_species)
taxa_df$ASV <- rownames(taxa_df)
taxa_df <- taxa_df[, c("ASV", setdiff(colnames(taxa_df), "ASV"))]

#  Save taxonomy table as a tab-separated file
write.table(taxa_df,
            file = "data/01_DADA2/ASV_taxonomy.tsv",
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

#  Intuition check - confirm ASV IDs are correctly labeled
print(head(taxa_df$ASV))
## [1] "ASV_0001" "ASV_0002" "ASV_0003" "ASV_0004" "ASV_0005" "ASV_0006"
# Save tracking object for downstream phyloseq integration
save(track_counts_df, file = "data/01_DADA2/track_read_counts.RData")
